decisions: Transport: 'local' -> LocalStreamSupervisor always; 'rtsp' -> RTSP if a CAMERA_ACCOUNT exists, else local; 'auto' -> RTSP if a CAMERA_ACCOUNT exists (keeps Phase 1 manual cameras on RTSP, as models.py documents), else local. Cloud cameras have no camera account, so they use :8800 like the phone app.

Local preview: resolution 'HD' for HD/TELE_HD, 'VGA' for SD/TELE_SD; channel 1 for TELE_* (second lens), else 0; port = media_port; password = CLOUD vault entry. LocalStreamSupervisor is called as factory(host, password, width, height, resolution=, port=, channel=, on_frame=, on_state=, limiter=, limiter_key=host).

TapoCameraService gained optional local_stream_factory / stream_factory / control_factory / alarm_poll_interval kwargs (defaults import the core classes lazily). control_factory is called with keyword args host=, password=, username=, port=, pin_store=.

lan_found False or empty host: start_stream -> on_state(FAILED, 'Not on this network'); connect(), start_events() and download_recording() raise TapoConnectionError('Not on this network') without network I/O.

Motion without a camera account: daemon thread polls getLastAlarmInfo every 5 s; the first reading is a baseline; each later change of last_alarm_time emits one active MotionEvent(source='last_alarm_info', topic='tapo:LastAlarmInfo/<type>'). Verified against the mock camera.

Cloud errors are recognised by class name in the MRO (CloudMfaRequired, CloudAuthError, CloudError) so account.py imports without core.cloud; network failures are TapoConnectionError. match_devices / normalise_mac are imported lazily from core.discovery.matcher with a built-in fallback implementing spec lan.match_rule.

Cloud cameras: id = deviceId, source 'cloud', host = LAN ip or '', https_port = LanDevice.http_port or 443, mac normalised. A successful cloud list also removes cloud cameras that left the account; an offline or failed list only updates LAN state of cached cameras. Manual cameras are never touched.

'Keep me signed in' off: no account secret and no 'account' setting are stored; per-camera CLOUD creds are stored for the session; at the next start restore_session() finds no account and removes those cloud cameras.
Silent sign-in that gets an MFA challenge opens SignInDialog on its MFA section. A failed silent sign-in (e.g. password changed) shows a status-bar message and keeps the cached cameras.
'Use without account' at startup is remembered (setting 'sign_in_skipped'), so the dialog is not forced on every start; signing in clears it. The account menu always offers 'Sign in...'.
Camera row text: name, plus ' (Offline)' (cloud online=False) or ' (Not on this network)'; the bare status is in Qt.UserRole+1. Manual cameras keep text == name (Phase 1 tests).
Snapshot: controller caches the newest delivered QImage per camera; PNG saved to %USERPROFILE%\Pictures\Tapo Desktop\<sanitised name>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>[_n].png; result shown in the status bar.
